context7_usage.reason: Pure repo-local synthesis: combines B276 autolaunch dryrun spec, B277 owner notification loop spec, and B275 completion_inbox.py into a unified queue-request -> launch -> completion-inbox -> stale-recovery -> usage-accounting flow. No external API/SDK question open.

builds_on: DEEPSEEK_TASK_MCP_AUTOLAUNCH_DRYRUN_SPEC_B276_V1 (command templates, 4-gate safety model, 15-field launch log, completion return path)
CLAUDE_TASK_MCP_OWNER_NOTIFICATION_LOOP_SPEC_B277_V1 (5-kind event taxonomy, delta cursor, automatic loop definition)
tools/geoai-task-mcp/src/geoai_task_mcp/completion_inbox.py (build_completion_inbox with 5 facets: review_queue, stale_processing, runner_mismatch_warnings, latest_validation_facts, read_errors)
summary: Synthesizes B276 (autolaunch) and B277 (notification loop) into a unified queue-request -> completion-inbox flow. Defines exactly how Codex creates a launch request (queue_request JSON envelope), how the MCP would process it through the 4-gate safety model, how completion_inbox reports results, how stale tasks are detected and recovered, and how usage accounting events flow back to the cost ledger. Every process-launch and notification-delivery capability remains at the design stage; no CLI/model process is launched by this artifact. All authority_flags are false. The queue_request schema is a pure JSON design that feeds into the existing auto_pickup + completion_inbox pipeline without introducing new subprocess paths.

section_1_queue_request_schema.title: Queue Request Creation (Codex -> MCP)
section_1_queue_request_schema.description: Codex creates a queue_request JSON object and deposits it via a proposed geoai_task_queue_request MCP tool (not implemented here). The schema is a self-describing envelope that the MCP autolauncher would consume to spawn workers through the B276 command templates behind the 4-gate safety model.

queue_request_envelope.request_id: string, deterministic sha1(task_id + runner + requested_at)[:16] — idempotent, same task+runner+timestamp = same request_id
queue_request_envelope.task_id: string, the task card id to launch a worker for
queue_request_envelope.runner: string, the runner name (e.g., claude_coding, deepseek_task_mcp_autolaunch_b281)
queue_request_envelope.topic: string, the task topic (e.g., coding, task_mcp)
queue_request_envelope.adapter: string enum: claude_cli | codex_cli | deepseek_manual — which B276 command template to use
queue_request_envelope.model: string, model identifier (e.g., claude-sonnet-4-5, gpt-5.5, deepseek-v4-pro)
queue_request_envelope.owner_prompt: string, the owner's instruction text to pass to the worker (may be empty for auto_pickup tasks)
queue_request_envelope.requested_at: string, ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when Codex created this request
queue_request_envelope.priority: string enum: critical | high | medium | low — mirrors task card priority
queue_request_envelope.max_turns: integer, max conversation turns for the worker (default 200)
queue_request_envelope.stale_timeout_seconds: integer, how long before the worker is considered stale (default 7200 for claude/codex, 86400 for deepseek_manual)
queue_request_envelope.env_overrides: object, optional env vars to set for the worker process (must not include secrets; audit-log sanitized per B276 G1)
queue_request_envelope.authority_flags: object, embedded per-request — always all-false in dryrun mode; mirrored from task card authority_flags for launch-time checks

transitions.created -> gated: request received by MCP, G1-G4 checks begin
transitions.gated -> launched: all 4 gates pass, process spawned via B276 adapter template
transitions.gated -> blocked: any gate fails, request recorded as blocked with failed_gate_ids
transitions.running -> completed: worker exits, completion_inbox detects review_queue entry
transitions.running -> failed: worker process exits with non-zero code or unrecoverable error

section_1_queue_request_schema.idempotency_rule: Same request_id submitted twice is a no-op if the previous request is still in created/gated/launched/running state. If the previous request reached completed/stale/failed, a new request with the same task_id is allowed (re-queue). This prevents double-launch of the same worker.

section_2_completion_inbox_integration.title: Completion Inbox Integration (MCP -> Codex)
section_2_completion_inbox_integration.description: After a worker finishes (or fails, or goes stale), the MCP autolauncher updates the task card lifecycle_state (via taskctl.py review for completion, or taskctl.py start for stale recovery). Codex's orchestration loop then detects the change through the EXISTING build_completion_inbox() facets — no new tool needed for the read path.

step_1_worker_finishes.action: Worker writes outputs to allowed_writes, runs taskctl.py review <task_id>

step_2_codex_detects.action: Codex orchestration loop calls geoai_completion_inbox() (existing tool) or proposed geoai_completion_inbox_delta() (B277 section_2b)
step_2_codex_detects.detection: review_queue entry has validation_status, runner_task_batch_mismatch, and allowed_writes list

step_3_codex_reviews.action: Codex runs taskctl.py guard-staged, inspects allowed_writes artifacts, checks validation_status
step_3_codex_reviews.outcome: PASS -> taskctl.py stage + git commit; FAIL -> create repair task

step_4_usage_accounting.action: Codex records usage via geoai_task_usage_report (existing tool) or reads from the 15-field launch log (B276 section_3)
step_4_usage_accounting.detection: usage_report() returns input/output tokens and cost_usd per task_id/runner

recovery_steps: 1. Codex detects stale entry via completion_inbox or proposed delta tool
2. Codex checks if a newer card already supersedes this task (git log --grep check)
3. If superseded: mark the stale task as finished/done via taskctl.py done
4. If genuinely abandoned: create a requeue_request with a new runner assignment, resetting lifecycle_state to pending
5. If the worker process is still alive (zombie): kill it (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 30s) before requeuing
stale_recovery_flow.zombie_kill_policy: The MCP autolauncher records the worker PID at launch time. On stale detection, it checks /proc/<pid> before killing. If the PID no longer exists, the task is marked stale-completed (process died silently).

collision_and_duplicate_runner_handling.trigger: build_completion_inbox()['runner_mismatch_warnings'] returns entries OR core.collision_guard() reports 2+ runners claiming the same task_id
handling: 1. Codex detects collision via geoai_task_collision_guard (existing tool) or completion_inbox runner_mismatch_warnings
2. For batch-token mismatch: the newer claim is authoritative if it passes taskctl guard; the older claim is marked stale
3. For same-task_id double-claim: the runner whose task card has the more recent claimed_at wins; the other claim is rejected with a collision_block entry
4. Codex creates a collision_report event (kind=duplicate_runner per B277 section_1) and pauses auto_pickup for that task_id
collision_and_duplicate_runner_handling.collision_prevention: Before creating a queue_request, Codex MUST run taskctl.py guard <task_id> --dryrun to verify the task is not already claimed. The queue_request idempotency rule (section_1) provides a second layer: same request_id re-submitted is a no-op.

section_3_usage_accounting_events.title: Usage Accounting Flow
section_3_usage_accounting_events.description: Every worker launch attempt records a 15-field launch log entry (B276 section_3). Additionally, Codex records per-task usage via geoai_task_usage_report (existing tool). This section defines how these two accounting sources reconcile into a unified cost ledger.

source_2_taskctl_usage.written_by: Codex or worker via taskctl.py usage

reconciliation_rules.prefer_launch_log_for_gate_events: G1-G4 gate check entries (gates_failed non-empty) are recorded ONLY in the launch log, not in taskctl usage (no process was spawned, no tokens consumed)
reconciliation_rules.prefer_taskctl_usage_for_token_counts: When a worker actually runs, taskctl.py usage records the final token counts; the launch log may have a preliminary estimate. Final cost_usd always comes from taskctl usage if available.
reconciliation_rules.cost_ledger_aggregation: A proposed geoai_task_cost_ledger MCP tool (not implemented here) would UNION both sources, deduplicate by (task_id, runner, model), and produce per-topic/per-runner/per-day aggregates. Until implemented, Codex aggregates manually from the two read-only sources.

usage_event_envelope.note: Matches B277 event_kind=usage payload exactly; source field distinguishes launch_log vs taskctl_usage

section_4_queue_flow_state_machine.title: End-to-End Queue Flow State Machine
section_4_queue_flow_state_machine.description: Combines the queue_request lifecycle (section_1), completion_inbox detection (section_2), stale recovery (section_2), and usage accounting (section_3) into a single state machine with exactly 9 states and 12 transitions.

states.PENDING: Task exists in task_queue_v1.sqlite, not yet claimed by any runner
states.CLAIMED: Task claimed by a runner via auto_pickup; lifecycle_state=processing
states.LAUNCH_REQUESTED: Codex created a queue_request for this task; MCP has not yet processed it
states.GATE_CHECK: MCP is running G1-G4 safety gates; if any fail -> BLOCKED
states.LAUNCHED: Worker process spawned via B276 adapter template; PID recorded
states.RUNNING: Worker process confirmed alive; completion_inbox would show no review_queue entry yet
states.COMPLETED: Worker ran taskctl.py review; completion_inbox review_queue now contains this task; awaiting Codex finalization
states.STALE: Worker process exceeded stale_timeout_seconds without completing; stale_processing facet detects this
states.BLOCKED: A gate failed or a collision was detected; task cannot proceed without manual intervention

transitions.trigger: Zombie process unkillable or task superseded
Codex review FAIL -> repair task created, original marked done
Manual owner unblock or gate fix

invariants: A task_id can be in at most one of {LAUNCHED, RUNNING} at any time (single-worker invariant)
A task_id in COMPLETED must have a review_queue entry with validation_status
A task_id in STALE must have stale_hours >= stale_processing_hours threshold
A task_id in BLOCKED must have at least one failed_gate_id or collision_report entry
The MCP autolauncher never spawns a process when LAUNCH_IMPLEMENTED=false (G4 gate is always FAIL in dryrun)

section_5_authority_flags.title: Authority Flags (ALL FALSE)
section_5_authority_flags.description: Every authority flag is explicitly false. This spec grants zero runtime, default, support, model, score, launch, or notification authority. It is a pure design/synthesis artifact.

remaining_gaps_not_solved_by_this_spec: NO_PROCESS_SPAWN_IMPLEMENTED: The MCP autolauncher's actual process-spawn code is deferred to CODEX_TASK_MCP_AUTOLAUNCH_WIRE_PROCESS_B279_V1 (B276 next_wave, G4 LAUNCH_IMPLEMENTED=true required)
NO_QUEUE_REQUEST_TOOL_REGISTERED: The geoai_task_queue_request MCP tool that Codex would call to deposit queue_request JSON is not implemented; this spec defines the schema only
NO_COST_LEDGER_TOOL: The geoai_task_cost_ledger tool for unified cost aggregation across launch log + taskctl usage is not implemented
NO_OWNER_DELIVERY_CHANNEL: Per B277 blocker 1, no email/Slack/desktop-notify target exists for stale/failure notifications
NO_TRUE_PUSH: Per B277 section_3 honest framing, all detection is pull-based (agent loop calls completion_inbox); no inotify/DB-trigger/daemon exists
NO_ARTIFACT_BODY_READ: Per B277 blocker 2, this spec operates on task-card metadata only, never artifact file contents
neural_bridge_note: This spec introduces no learned decision authority and no regex/keyword cue router. The queue_flow state machine is a deterministic support-boundary mapping: each transition is triggered by an already-defined event (auto_pickup, taskctl review, stale timeout, gate check, collision_guard output). The 9 states and 12 transitions are a formalization of the existing taskctl lifecycle + B276/B277 protocols. If a future task teaches a controller to PRIORITIZE which task to launch next or SELECT which adapter to use, that becomes a neural curriculum target per neural_bridge_priority (see mcp_neural_launch_routing_migration_b254_v1); this task only defines the deterministic state machine it would operate within.
